dimensions.assessment: Affects Department of Labor employees (such as those in the Wage and Hour Division) designated to receive human trafficking detection training.
dimensions.evidence: employees of the Department of Labor whom the Secretary determines should receive such training or education

dimensions.assessment: Mandates specialized training, continuing education, and case reporting procedures for relevant agency staff.
dimensions.evidence: implement a program to provide the training and periodic continuing education... to employees of the Department of Labor

dimensions.assessment: The source material does not outline specific costs or funding authorizations for the training program.
Imposes new agency-wide training duties and annual congressional reporting requirements on the Department of Labor.
dimensions.evidence: the Secretary of Labor shall implement a program to provide the training and periodic continuing education

dimensions.assessment: Requires ongoing periodic continuing education and annual reports to congressional committees indefinitely.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than 1 year after the Secretary of Labor first implements the program... and each year thereafter

missing_information: Estimated implementation cost or funding required for the employee training programs
importance_detail.rationale: The bill requires the Department of Labor to implement training and continuing education programs for certain employees to detect and assist law enforcement in preventing human trafficking, and to submit annual reports to Congress.
